title: Forgiving everyone
hook: an ordinary man, promised Paradise, who did nothing special except sleep with no grudge
tomorrow: why did someone stay behind in Mecca on the night of the escape?

segments.voice: Yesterday: what continues. Charity that keeps flowing, knowledge someone still uses, a child who prays. Today the week comes back, and one more thing to put down.

Some people fall asleep the moment their head hits the pillow, and it can feel deeply unfair. In a report in Musnad Ahmad, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tells his companions that a man of Paradise is about to walk in, and an ordinary man of the Ansar walks in. A young companion, Abdullah ibn Amr, wants the secret. He finds a reason to stay at the man's house and watch. He sees nothing special: no all-night prayers. Just a man who remembers Allah when he turns over in bed, and sleeps.
screen: `ASLEEP THE MOMENT HE LIES DOWN.` → `A MAN OF PARADISE WALKS IN.` → `NOTHING SPECIAL. HE SLEEPS.`

segments.voice: So Abdullah asks him outright. The man says: it's only what you saw, except that I keep no grudge in my heart against any Muslim, and I don't envy anyone for the good Allah has given them. Abdullah says: that is what got you there. Forgiving everyone isn't a speech. It's a nightly putting-down, and it doesn't wait for the other person to go first. The report names fellow Muslims; the Qur'an's line on forgiving reaches wider, in Pickthall's words: "let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you?" Now the week comes back as one road. Committed: a small rule, signed. A pilgrimage: leave, circle, stand, return. Just passing: a light bag. Loves to meet him: a meeting you get ready for. Think well: hope leads at the end. What continues: good that outlives you. And the lightest thing to carry into sleep is nothing at all.
screen: `NO GRUDGE, NO ENVY.` · `A NIGHTLY PUTTING-DOWN.` · `YEARN YE NOT TO BE FORGIVEN?` · `THE WEEK, ONE ROAD.` · then, large: `NO GRUDGE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person you're still holding something against, even a little. Breathe out slowly and, for this one breath, set it down; you don't have to call them or pretend it didn't happen. If it comes back, set it down again.
screen: `ONE PERSON, ONE GRUDGE.` · `BREATHE OUT, SET IT DOWN.` · `AGAIN, IF IT COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: Forgiving everyone: letting go of grudges and envy, every night, so you can sleep with a clear heart.
Two words for the pillow tonight: no grudge, set down before you sleep. Sleep well, and see you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1771 COUNTS.` → `THE JOURNEY HOME · 6 OF 11.` → `TOMORROW: WHO STAYED BEHIND ON THE NIGHT OF THE ESCAPE?`

howItsDone: Some Muslims make a habit of forgiving everyone before they sleep, pointing to this report in Musnad Ahmad; Qur'an 24:22 is often recited as a reason to forgive.

Abdullah saw nothing special. the man's secret: no grudge, no envy.
forgiving in Islam means pretending it never happened
the practice is setting the grudge down; nothing says you must pretend or fully trust again.

fork.setup: you keep replaying a coworker's rude comment every night, and it's costing you sleep. what does the man of Paradise's habit point to?
options: set the grudge down before sleep, every night it comes back.
wait to forgive until she apologizes; then let it go.
pray longer at night so the good outweighs the anger.
fork.reveal: he did nothing special except keep no grudge in his heart. forgiving here is a nightly putting-down, not a reward for an apology.

original.note: Arabic: pardon, letting a wrong go; the Qur'an uses this root in 24:22.

trapdoor: what you thought: forgiving everyone means saying everything's fine.
what it means: putting down grudges and envy, nightly, so the heart is clear; the man of Paradise did nothing more.
what a scholar hears: Musnad Ahmad 12697 (Anas), Abdullah ibn Amr's stay; 'against any Muslim' in the report, read with 24:22, revealed about forgiving a relative who had wronged Abu Bakr's family.
guess: letting go of grudges and envy, every night
agreeing that whatever someone did was all right
asking each person you've hurt to forgive you

chat.says: Dadi called an old friend she fell out with. no apology, just 'salaam, how are your knees?' is that it?
options: Could be. Forgiving can be quiet: the grudge set down, like the man of Paradise.
Not really. It only counts once the other person apologizes and admits what she did.
No. Real forgiving means acting like nothing happened and trusting her fully again.
chat.meaning: In Ahmad's report, the man promised Paradise did nothing special except keep no grudge or envy. Forgiving can be a quiet putting-down.

Musnad Ahmad.meaning: a large collection of hadith gathered by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal

Ansar.meaning: the Muslims of Medina who welcomed the Prophet

Abdullah ibn Amr.meaning: a young companion of the Prophet

Pickthall.meaning: a public-domain English translation of the Qur'an

sources.ref: Musnad Ahmad 12697 (from Anas): a man of the Ansar is called a man of Paradise; Abdullah ibn Amr stays with him and finds nothing special except that he holds no grudge against any Muslim and envies no one
